::: {.callout-warning}
## Read before quoting a number
One Windows laptop (i7-11390H, 31.8 GB RAM), R single-threaded on reference BLAS, ten
cold trials per configuration, medians. Some configurations were disturbed by other
processes and are labelled as such below. **No result transfers to other hardware**; the
second benchmark platform is an open roadmap item. The benchmark does not assume Rust
wins, and on random forests it does not.
:::

## Headline ranges

Computed at build time from the per-trial CSVs of the Phase 5 protocol runs
(`benchmarks/results/<run>/results.csv`, runs G–K of 2026-10-13/14: 10 cold trials,
30 warm iterations, 10 folds, 20-point or 4 × 5 grids), not copied from prose. Each
cell is the range of R median / native median over the tasks of that family at **one
thread**; the task behind each end of a range is named. The same script fails the
build if the README's summary paragraph disagrees with these numbers.

{{< include generated/benchmarks-headline.md >}}

The random-forest row is the one to read first: the port is **on par with ranger, not
faster**, and R is faster on one of the two CV cells. The 1.1× lower end of the
logistic tuning row is 100k rows against glmnet, a different algorithm. An earlier
version of the README and of this page quoted 6–930× for linear and logistic fits
(the 6× was OLS; logistic at 1e6 rows is 3.4×) and a Python wrapper "within ±5%" that
the data does not support; both were corrected on 2026-10-14 after this recomputation
(`LIMITATIONS.md`).

Two categories are kept apart in every table: **framework-overhead**, where both sides
run the same algorithm (`lm`, `glm`, rpart, xgboost against their ports) and a ratio
measures orchestration plus solver; and **workflow-level**, where the algorithms differ
(ranger against the forest port, glmnet's path against one IRLS per candidate) and a
ratio is never described as like for like.

### Four threads

R runs `fit_resamples` with `future::plan(multisession)`, whose worker start-up is
inside the timed phase; Rust and Python use the framework's thread pool.

## Before/after for merged optimisations

Any optimisation merged into the library has an interleaved A/B against the
pre-optimisation build with bitwise-identical outputs as the acceptance condition; the
record is `docs/perf/2026-10-13-rust-opts-ab.md` in the repository
([Design decisions](decisions.qmd) lists the related ADRs).
